title: URL shortener
prompt: Design a URL shortening service. Users submit a long URL and get back a short link; anyone who opens the short link is redirected to the original.
hard_part: Unique short codes at scale; read-heavy traffic
key_points: Picked a short-code scheme (counter + base62, random with a unique insert, or a hash) and named its trade-off
Chose 301 or 302 on purpose and said what it costs (browser caching vs analytics, edits and takedowns)
Scaled the redirect path with a cache (and optionally the CDN), including brief negative caching for missing codes
Checked expiry at read time and never reused codes
Covered abuse: rate-limited creation, scanned destinations, could disable a code instantly
Kept analytics off the redirect path (asynchronous click events)
